Lower your chest towards the floor with your body in a straight line, then press back up. Your hands stay planted, so your wrists are loaded in extension.
Press the handles forward while keeping your upper back supported against the pad.
Lying on a bench, press two dumbbells from chest height to straight arms. The dumbbells let your elbows travel further down than a barbell would.
Press two dumbbells upwards from an inclined bench. The angle shifts work towards the upper chest and front shoulders.
Lying on a bench, lower a barbell to your chest and press it back up. The fixed bar sets your grip width and holds your wrists in extension.
With a slight bend in your elbows, bring both cable handles together in front of your chest. Your arms open wide at the start of each rep.
Seated with your thighs secured, pull the bar down to your upper chest, then let it rise under control.
Pull yourself up to the bar with the machine counterweighting part of your bodyweight, so you can pick the load.
Hang from the bar and pull until your chin clears it. Your full bodyweight loads your shoulders, elbows, and grip.
Sitting tall, pull the handle to your stomach and return under control. Reaching forward at the start rounds your lower back under load.
Lying face down on an inclined bench, row two dumbbells towards your hips. The bench carries your torso, so your lower back is not loaded.
Row one handle at a time against a chest pad, so each side works independently while the machine supports your torso.
Hinged forward with a flat back, row the barbell to your stomach. Holding the hinge under load is the hard part of this exercise.
Anchor a band at chest height, step back to tension it, and pull the handles to your ribs.
Press the handles overhead with your back against the pad.
Press two dumbbells from shoulder height to overhead while seated with back support.
Raise two dumbbells out to your sides up to shoulder height, leading with your elbows.
Raise a low cable handle out to the side, one arm at a time, for constant tension through the range.
Standing on a band, raise the handles out to your sides up to shoulder height.
With the cables crossed in front of you, pull both handles out and back to work the rear shoulders.
Pull a rope towards your face at eye level, rotating your hands outwards as your elbows travel back.
Hold a band at chest height with straight arms and pull it apart until it touches your sternum.
Curl two dumbbells from your sides to your shoulders with your palms turned up.
Curl two dumbbells with your palms facing each other, keeping your forearms in a neutral position throughout.
Curl a low cable bar to your shoulders with your palms turned up, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Standing on a band, curl the handles to your shoulders with your palms turned up.
With your elbows at your sides and palms facing down, press the bar down until your arms are straight.
Facing away from the cable with your arms overhead, straighten your elbows against the resistance.
Anchor a band overhead and press the handles down until your elbows are straight, palms facing down.
Lower and press yourself back up between the handles with the machine counterweighting part of your bodyweight.
Supporting your full bodyweight on parallel bars, lower until your upper arms are level with your torso, then press back up. Your shoulders travel behind your body at the bottom.
Sit down and back between your feet, then stand tall again. Depth is up to you.
Hold one dumbbell at your chest and squat down between your feet. The load sits in front of you, so your knees and hips both travel through a deep range.
Seated in the machine, press the platform away until your legs are almost straight. Your back stays supported throughout.
Seated in the machine, straighten your knees against the pad. All of the load goes through the knee joint.
With your rear foot on a bench, lower straight down on the front leg and drive back up. One leg carries the work and your balance.
Step forward and lower your back knee towards the floor, then step through onto the other leg.
Step onto a bench with one leg and stand up on it, then lower under control. The working leg does the work; the other only guides you.
Holding two dumbbells, push your hips back and lower the weights along your legs with a flat back, then stand tall. Your back holds its position against the load.
Balancing on one leg, hinge forward and lower a dumbbell towards the floor, then return upright. Your standing leg carries both the load and your balance.
Seated with your hips bent, pull your heels down and under the seat against the pad.
Lying face down, curl your heels towards your glutes against the pad.
Kneeling with your ankles anchored, lower your torso towards the floor as slowly as you can, then pull yourself back up. Your knees carry your weight throughout.
Lying on your back with your knees bent, drive your hips up until your body is level from knees to shoulders.
With your upper back on a bench and a barbell across your hips, drive your hips up to full extension and lower under control.
Facing away from a low cable, push your hips back to let the rope travel between your legs, then stand tall by driving your hips forward.
Seated in the machine, press your knees outwards against the pads and return under control.
With a band around your thighs, press your knees apart against the resistance.
Seated in the machine, squeeze your knees together against the pads. Each rep starts with your legs held apart.
Standing on one leg with a band around the other ankle, pull that leg across your body against the resistance.
Standing tall, rise onto the balls of your feet and lower your heels under control.
Seated with the pad across your thighs, rise onto the balls of your feet and lower your heels under control.
Lying on your back, extend one arm and the opposite leg away from you while keeping your lower back flat on the floor.
On hands and knees, reach one arm and the opposite leg out without letting your hips rotate.
Hold a straight line from head to heels on your forearms and toes. Hold each set for 20–45 seconds.
On one forearm, hold your body in a straight line without letting your hips drop. Hold each set for 20–45 seconds per side.
Standing side-on to a cable, press the handle straight out from your chest and resist the pull that tries to rotate you.
Kneeling below a high cable, curl your ribs towards your hips against the load, then return under control.
Hanging from a bar, draw your knees up towards your chest and lower them without swinging.
